item.title: Credit Corporation contributes $30,000 to support free heart care
item.description: Children and adults who need heart treatment will continue to receive care free of charge at the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital, with Credit Corporation contributing $30,000 in support over the next three years. The company's Country Manager Mohammed Nawaz and his executive team handed over the first $10,000 contribution to Hospital Director Dr Krupali Tappoo on 20th October.
item.content:encoded:
Children and adults who need heart treatment will continue to receive care free of charge at the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital, with Credit Corporation contributing $30,000 in support over the next three years.

The company's Country Manager Mohammed Nawaz and his executive team handed over the first $10,000 contribution to Hospital Director Dr Krupali Tappoo on 20th October.

Nawaz says heart disease affects many families in Fiji, and the cost of treatment can make it difficult for some people to access the care they need.

He says the hospital has shown what is possible when care is provided to everyone, regardless of their financial circumstances, and Credit Corporation is proud to support its work.

The company will provide $10,000 each year for three years to help meet the hospital's operating costs.

Hospital Director and CEO Dr Krupali Tappoo says support from businesses is important as the need for specialised cardiac care across Fiji and the Pacific continues to grow.

D evelopment and Partnerships Manager Stephanie Lenert says support from the corporate sector helps the hospital continue providing life-saving care to children and families across the region.

Dr Tappoo says established in April 2022 by Sai Prema Foundation Fiji, the hospital is the Pacific's first specialist cardiac hospital, providing consultations, diagnostic tests, interventions and surgeries free of charge.

She adds as of October this year, the hospital has provided 553 free heart surgeries and interventions, 59,855 echocardiograms and 142,906 specialist and general medical consultations.

Its paediatric cardiac programme has treated children from Fiji, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Tonga, Samoa, Kiribati, Tuvalu, Christmas Island and Papua New Guinea.

Dr Tappoo adds the hospital is also expanding its free services to include adult cardiac care and advanced cardiac interventions, helping people access treatment without having to travel overseas at significant cost.

item.title: FNPF Acting Chief Operations Officer Emily King joins Merchant Finance Board
item.description: Fiji National Provident Fund's Acting Chief Operations Officer, Emily King has been appointed to the Board of Merchant Finance Pte Limited. King who previously served as its General Counsel brings more than 15 years of experience in corporate law, governance, risk management and financial services.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji National Provident Fund's Acting Chief Operations Officer, Emily King has been appointed to the Board of Merchant Finance Pte Limited.

King who previously served as its General Counsel brings more than 15 years of experience in corporate law, governance, risk management and financial services.

She has experience in regulatory compliance, enterprise risk management, board governance and organizational strategy.

Merchant Finance Board Chairperson Isikeli Tikoduadua says King’s experience across legal, governance, risk and regulatory disciplines will be a valuable addition to the Board.

Tikoduadua says the Board looks forward to the insights and leadership she will bring as the company strengthens its governance framework and supports sustainable business growth.

King’s appointment took effect on 6th of this month.

Merchant Finance says the appointment reflects its commitment to maintaining a skilled and diverse Board to support its long-term strategic objectives.

The Board now comprises Tikoduadua as Chairperson, Sereana Matakibau, Jaoji Koroi, Cecil Browne, Sala Toganivalu-Lesuma, Narendra Kumar and King.

The company says it remains committed to maintaining an appropriate balance of skills, experience, independence and diversity to provide effective oversight and strategic direction.

item.title: Edwin Shankar appointed ANZ Kiribati Country Head
item.description: Fijian banker, Edwin Shankar has been appointed the new Country Head of ANZ Kiribati, subject to regulatory approvals, and is expected to take up the role in early December. Shankar is currently Director Diversified Industries with ANZ Papua New Guinea and has more than 20 years of banking experience across Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Solomon Islands, Australia and the wider Pacific.
item.content:encoded:
Fijian banker, Edwin Shankar has been appointed the new Country Head of ANZ Kiribati, subject to regulatory approvals, and is expected to take up the role in early December.

Shankar is currently Director Diversified Industries with ANZ Papua New Guinea and has more than 20 years of banking experience across Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Solomon Islands, Australia and the wider Pacific.

He will report to ANZ Vanuatu Country Head Sucharu Tandon and succeed Greg Edwards, who has led ANZ Kiribati since 2019.

ANZ Regional Executive Pacific Sarah Stubbings says Shankar’s regional experience, customer relationships and leadership skills will be valuable in the role.

Stubbings says Kiribati remains an important market for ANZ, which is the country’s only commercial bank.

She says the bank remains committed to providing safe, reliable and accessible banking services while investing in its people, expanding digital access and supporting financial inclusion.

Shankar says he is privileged to be appointed to the role and looks forward to meeting customers, colleagues and stakeholders.

Earlier in his career, he served as Head of Treasury and Trade in Solomon Islands and held money market, balance sheet and foreign exchange roles in Fiji.

He holds an MBA Global with Distinction from James Cook University.

Stubbings has also thanked Edwards for his leadership, saying he helped maintain continuity of banking services through a period of significant change .

ANZ says Shankar will undertake a structured handover to ensure continuity for customers, colleagues and stakeholders.
